title: Groenland–Joret–Nadara–Walczak Conjecture on treedepth vs. pathwidth
statement_text: Every graph of pathwidth less than $a$ containing no $2^b$-vertex path has treedepth $O(ab)$.
context_text: Theorem 1 (Czerwiński, Nadara, Pilipczuk) had previously given a bound of $O(a^2 b)$ for such graphs by combining treewidth and binary-tree-minor bounds. The authors of [5] conjectured the bound could be reduced to $O(ab)$, matching the natural product of the two parameters.
paper_contribution: Proves the conjecture by establishing Theorem 3: every graph of pathwidth less than $a$ containing no $2^b$-vertex path has treedepth at most $10ab$, and shows this bound is tight up to a constant factor.

title: Open Problem: sharpness of the treedepth bound in Theorem 1
statement_text: Czerwiński, Nadara and Pilipczuk proved that every graph of treewidth less than $t$ with no complete binary tree of height $h$ as a minor and no $2^b$-vertex path (as a subgraph) has treedepth $O(thb)$. Whether this bound $O(thb)$ can be improved remains an open problem.
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple; paths are not required to be induced. Treedepth $\mathrm{td}(G)$ is the minimum height of a rooted forest $F$ on $V(G)$ such that every edge of $G$ joins a vertex to one of its ancestors in $F$; one has $\mathrm{tw}(G)+1\le\mathrm{pw}(G)+1\le\mathrm{td}(G)$. Each parameter is approximated by an obstruction: treedepth by the longest path (a graph with an $\ell$-vertex path has treedepth greater than $\log_2\ell$, and one with no such path has treedepth less than $\ell$), pathwidth by the largest height of a complete binary tree minor, treewidth by the largest grid minor. Kawarabayashi and Rossman showed that every graph of treewidth less than $k$ with no height-$k$ complete binary tree minor and no $2^k$-vertex path has treedepth $O(k^5\log^2 k)$, and the bound $O(thb)$ above improves this (it is stated by its authors for $t=h=b$, but the proof works in general). It also follows by combining two results: Groenland, Joret, Nadara and Walczak proved that treewidth less than $t$ and no complete binary tree minor of height $h$ give pathwidth $O(th)$, and the present paper proves that every graph of pathwidth less than $a$ with no $2^b$-vertex path has treedepth at most $10ab$. Each of these two bounds is sharp up to a constant factor (for the second, blow up each vertex of a path on $2^{b-c}$ vertices into a clique of size $a/2=2^{c-1}$ and each edge into a complete bipartite graph), but it is unknown whether their combination $O(thb)$ is optimal.
